title: Primes of a localized polynomial fibre are irreducible factors
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $f,g\in R[t]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], with $f$ monic (leading coefficient $1$), and put $A=R[t]/(f)$ and $B=A_{g_A}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], where $g_A$ is the class of $g$. Let $\mathfrak q$ be a prime ideal of $B$ and $\mathfrak p$ its contraction to $R$. Put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and let $\rho:R[t]\to k[t]$ apply $R\to k$ to each coefficient. Write $f_k=\rho(f)$, $g_k=\rho(g)$ and $F=(k[t]/(f_k))_{[g_k]}$, with the canonical map $j:B\to F$. There is a unique monic irreducible polynomial $h\in k[t]$ (irreducible means nonzero and not a unit, and every factorization has a unit factor) such that $h\mid f_k$, $h\nmid g_k$, and $\mathfrak q=j^{-1}(((h)/(f_k))F)$. Here $(h)/(f_k)$ is the image of the ideal $(h)$ in $k[t]/(f_k)$ and the trailing $F$ denotes extension of this ideal to $F$. Explicitly, for every $P\in R[t]$ and $m\ge0$, one has $[P]/g_A^m\in\mathfrak q$ if and only if $h\mid\rho(P)$ in $k[t]$.

proof.text: Put $L=\kappa(\mathfrak q)=B_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q}$, and write $\tau:B\to L$ for the residue map [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Its kernel is exactly $\mathfrak q$: membership in $\mathfrak q$ plainly gives zero; conversely, if $b/1$ is in $\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q}$, write a finite sum of its ideal generators over a common denominator $s\notin\mathfrak q$. The fraction-equality rule gives $ub s\in\mathfrak q$ for another $u\notin\mathfrak q$, and primality gives $b\in\mathfrak q$. Thus the composite $R\to B\xrightarrow{\tau}L$ has kernel $\mathfrak p$, and every $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ has nonzero image in $L$. In particular $L$ and $k$ are nonzero fields.

source.place: Tag 00UF, lemma-standard-etale-finite-flat-Zariski, proof, residue-field paragraph beginning Let overline f denote the image of f; the prime/factor identification expanded.

proof.text: Using the fractions of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], define $\iota:k\to L$ by $\iota(\overline{r/s})=\tau(r)/\tau(s)$ for $s\notin\mathfrak p$, where $r,s$ on the right denote their images in $B$. Fraction equality and reduction modulo $\mathfrak p$ preserve this formula because the composite $R\to L$ kills exactly $\mathfrak p$; its kernel on $k$ is zero since $\tau(r)=0$ precisely when $r\in\mathfrak p$. Let $x=\tau([t]/1)$, and define $\theta:k[t]\to L$ by $\theta(\sum_i a_it^i)=\sum_i\iota(a_i)x^i$, using the coefficient operations of [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Then $\theta\rho(P)=\tau([P]/1)$ for every $P\in R[t]$. Consequently $Q=\ker\theta$ is a proper prime ideal (a product evaluates to zero in the field $L$ only if a factor does), $f_k\in Q$, and $g_k\notin Q$, since $[g]/1$ is a unit in $B$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. The polynomial $f_k$ is nonzero: its leading coefficient is the image of $1$, hence still $1$.

source.place: Tag 00UF, lemma-standard-etale-finite-flat-Zariski, proof, residue-field paragraph beginning Let overline f denote the image of f; the prime/factor identification expanded.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-polynomial-field-pid] to the field $k$. It gives an integral domain $k[t]$ and a polynomial $d$ with $Q=(d)$. Since $f_k\in Q$ is nonzero, $d\ne0$; since $Q$ is proper, $d$ is not a unit.

source.place: Tag 00UF, lemma-standard-etale-finite-flat-Zariski, proof, residue-field paragraph beginning Let overline f denote the image of f; the prime/factor identification expanded.

proof.text: Let $c\in k^\times$ be the leading coefficient of $d$ and put $h=c^{-1}d$. From the coefficient definition [def-weil-polynomial-ring], $h$ is monic and $(h)=(d)=Q$. It is nonzero and not a unit. If $h=uv$, primality of $Q$ puts one of $u,v$ in $(h)$. If $u=ha$, cancellation of the nonzero $h$ in $h=hav$ gives $av=1$, so $v$ is a unit; the other case is symmetric. Thus $h$ is irreducible. The relations $f_k\in(h)$ and $g_k\notin(h)$ are precisely $h\mid f_k$ and $h\nmid g_k$.

source.place: Tag 00UF, lemma-standard-etale-finite-flat-Zariski, proof, residue-field paragraph beginning Let overline f denote the image of f; the prime/factor identification expanded.

proof.text:
For $P\in R[t]$ and $m\ge0$, [def-weil-ring-localization-away] gives $\tau([P]/g_A^m)=\theta(\rho(P))/\theta(g_k)^m$. Its denominator is nonzero, so Step 1 and $\ker\theta=(h)$ give
$$[P]/g_A^m\in\mathfrak q\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\theta(\rho(P))=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h\mid\rho(P).$$
This proves the explicit membership clause, for every representative and every denominator exponent, including $m=0$.

source.place: Tag 00UF, lemma-standard-etale-finite-flat-Zariski, proof, residue-field paragraph beginning Let overline f denote the image of f; the prime/factor identification expanded.

proof.text: Since $\theta(f_k)=0$ and $\theta(g_k)\ne0$, evaluation gives a map $e:F\to L$ with $e([U]/[g_k]^m)=\theta(U)/\theta(g_k)^m$; the quotient relation and the fraction-equality rule [def-weil-ring-localization-away] make this well-defined. Its kernel is $I=((h)/(f_k))F$. Indeed the image of $h$ maps to zero, so $I\subseteq\ker e$; conversely $e([U]/[g_k]^m)=0$ implies $U\in Q=(h)$, say $U=hV$, and the fraction is the image of $h$ times $[V]/[g_k]^m$. The formulas give $ej=\tau$ on every $[P]/g_A^m$. Hence $j^{-1}(I)=\ker\tau=\mathfrak q$, proving the asserted equality of ideals.

source.place: Tag 00UF, lemma-standard-etale-finite-flat-Zariski, proof, residue-field paragraph beginning Let overline f denote the image of f; the prime/factor identification expanded.

proof.text:
For uniqueness, let $h'$ be any monic irreducible polynomial satisfying $h'\mid f_k$, $h'\nmid g_k$ and $j^{-1}(I')=\mathfrak q$, where $I'=((h')/(f_k))F$. Every common divisor of $h'$ and $g_k$ is a unit: a nonunit divisor of the irreducible $h'$ is associated to $h'$ and would force $h'\mid g_k$. Thus [def-weil-coprime-polynomials] gives that $h'$ and $g_k$ are coprime. Repeated application of [lem-weil-coprime-divides-product] gives $h'\mid g_k^NU$ if and only if $h'\mid U$, for every $N\ge0$. Now $[U]/1\in I'$ if and only if $h'\mid U$. The reverse implication is immediate. For the forward implication, $I'$ is the principal ideal generated by the class of $h'$, so write $[U]/1=[h'V]/[g_k]^m$. Fraction equality [def-weil-ring-localization-away] yields $g_k^N(g_k^mU-h'V)\in(f_k)$ for some $N$. Since $h'\mid f_k$, we get $h'\mid g_k^{N+m}U$ and cancel these factors by the preceding divisibility implication. In particular, for every $P\in R[t]$,
$$h'\mid\rho(P)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad[P]/1\in\mathfrak q\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h\mid\rho(P),$$
where the middle equivalence uses the assumed contraction and Step 5.

This uses exactly the fraction model of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and finite coefficient description [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. The scalar $\overline{s}$ is a nonzero constant, hence a unit in $k[t]$. Applying Step 7 to $P$ therefore shows $h'\mid U$ if and only if $h\mid U$ for every $U$. In particular $h\mid h'$ and $h'\mid h$. Write $h'=ha$ and $h=h'b$; cancellation in the domain gives $ab=1$. The coefficient formula shows that degrees of nonzero polynomial products add (the top coefficient is the product of the two nonzero top coefficients); hence $a,b$ are constants. Comparing the leading coefficients of the two monic polynomials gives $a=1$. Thus $h'=h$, as required.
